learn.hook: Banana peels, chips packets, old newspapers... Is all garbage the same? No way!
points: Waste is anything we throw away because we do not need it any more.
Wet waste comes from plants and food, like peels, leftover food, tea leaves and fallen leaves. It rots and mixes with the soil.
Dry waste includes paper, plastic, glass, metal and old cloth. Most of it does not rot quickly.
Plastic does not rot. It can stay in the soil and water for a very, very long time.
Some waste, like old batteries, medicines and broken bulbs, is harmful and must be handed over carefully by an adult.

example.q: A banana peel and a plastic wrapper are left in the garden for many weeks. What happens to each?
steps: The banana peel comes from a plant. Tiny living things break it down.
It slowly rots and mixes with the soil.
The plastic wrapper does not rot. It stays almost the same for years.
example.answer: The peel rots and mixes with soil; the plastic wrapper stays as it is

learn.reallife: Look at your kitchen dustbin after dinner. How much of it is wet waste and how much is dry?

games.title: Waste facts
items: A banana peel rots and mixes with the soil.
Tiny living things in the soil break it down.
Plastic bags rot in a few days.
Plastic does not rot. It stays for a very long time.
Paper is dry waste and can be recycled.

Burning garbage makes smoke that dirties the air.

quiz.q: Which of these is wet waste?
quiz.explain: Vegetable peels come from plants and rot easily, so they are wet waste.
steps: Wet waste comes from plants and food.
Vegetable peels rot easily.
So peels are wet waste.
Answer: Vegetable peels
quiz.mistake: Mixes up wet and dry waste

quiz.q: Which of these is dry waste?
quiz.explain: Paper is dry waste. The others are food waste, which is wet waste.
steps: Dry waste includes paper, plastic, glass and metal.
Dal, mango peel and tea leaves are wet waste.
So an old newspaper is dry waste.
Answer: An old newspaper
quiz.mistake: Mixes up wet and dry waste

quiz.q: What happens to a banana peel left in the soil for some weeks?
options: It rots and mixes with the soil
It stays the same for years
quiz.explain: Tiny living things in the soil break down the peel.
steps: Wet waste rots and mixes with the soil.
A banana peel is wet waste.
So it rots and mixes with the soil.
Answer: It rots and mixes with the soil
quiz.mistake: Thinks all waste stays forever

quiz.q: Why is plastic harmful when thrown on the ground?
options: It turns into food for plants
It does not rot and can harm animals
quiz.explain: Plastic stays for a very long time. Animals can eat it by mistake and get sick.
steps: Plastic does not rot.
It stays a very long time, and animals may eat it.
So it is harmful.
Answer: It does not rot and can harm animals
quiz.mistake: Thinks plastic breaks down like food waste

quiz.q: Which of these should be handed over carefully by an adult and not mixed with other waste?
quiz.explain: Batteries have harmful things inside, so they need special care.
steps: Old batteries, medicines and broken bulbs are harmful waste.
They must be handed over carefully by an adult.
So the answer is old batteries.
Answer: Old batteries
quiz.mistake: Does not know some waste is harmful

quiz.q: Why should we not burn garbage?
options: The smoke dirties the air and is bad for our health
quiz.explain: Burning garbage, especially plastic, gives off harmful smoke.
steps: Burning garbage makes smoke.
The smoke dirties the air and is bad for health.
So we should not burn garbage.
Answer: The smoke dirties the air and is bad for our health
quiz.mistake: Thinks burning is a safe way to get rid of waste

quiz.q: What is waste?
options: Things we throw away because we do not need them
quiz.explain: Waste is anything we throw away after use.
steps: Waste is anything we throw away.
We throw it because we do not need it any more.
So that is waste.
Answer: Things we throw away because we do not need them
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word waste

quiz.q: Riya's family throws away 5 bags of wet waste and 3 bags of dry waste in a week. How many more bags of wet waste than dry waste is that?
quiz.explain: 5 − 3 = 2 more bags of wet waste.
steps: Wet waste: 5 bags
Dry waste: 3 bags
Answer: 2

teach.ask: Gappu found a peel and a plastic packet. He asks: are they the same kind of waste?
teach.praise: Tweet! The peel rots, but plastic stays. They are different!
teach.nudge: Which waste rots and mixes with the soil?

revise.summary: Waste is what we throw away. Wet waste from food and plants rots and mixes with soil; dry waste like paper, plastic, glass and metal does not rot quickly. Plastic does not rot, and some waste is harmful.
focus: What happens to peels and plastic over time
Harmful waste and why not to burn garbage
remember: Wet waste: peels, leftover food, tea leaves, fallen leaves
Dry waste: paper, plastic, glass, metal, old cloth
Batteries, medicines and broken bulbs must be handed over by an adult
traps: Paper is dry waste even though it comes from trees.
Burning garbage is not a good way to get rid of it; the smoke is harmful.

learn.hook: Two bins can save the Earth a lot of trouble! Let's learn to sort our waste.
points: Keep wet waste and dry waste in separate bins at home and school.
In many cities, the green bin is for wet waste and the blue bin is for dry waste.
Sorted wet waste can be turned into compost, a rich manure for plants.
To make compost, put wet waste in a pit or a pot, cover it with soil or dry leaves, and wait some weeks.
Earthworms and tiny living things break the waste down into compost.

example.q: Why is it a good idea to keep wet and dry waste in separate bins?
steps: Wet waste can be turned into compost.
Dry waste like paper, glass and metal can be sent for recycling.
If they are mixed, the wet waste makes the dry waste dirty and both become hard to use.
example.answer: So wet waste can become compost and dry waste can be recycled

learn.reallife: Help your family keep two bins in the kitchen — one for wet waste and one for dry waste.

games.title: Making compost
items: Put them in a compost pot or pit
Cover with soil or dry leaves

quiz.q: In many Indian cities, which colour bin is used for wet waste?
quiz.explain: Green bins are for wet waste and blue bins are for dry waste.
steps: In many cities, the green bin is for wet waste.
The blue bin is for dry waste.
So the answer is green.
Answer: Green
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the bin colours

quiz.q: What is compost?
options: A rich manure made from rotted wet waste
quiz.explain: Compost is made when wet waste rots. It makes soil rich for plants.
steps: Wet waste can be turned into compost.
Compost is a rich manure for plants.
So that is compost.
Answer: A rich manure made from rotted wet waste
quiz.mistake: Does not know what compost is

quiz.q: Which of these can go into a compost pit?
quiz.explain: Vegetable peels rot and become compost. Plastic, glass and metal do not.
steps: Only wet waste goes into a compost pit.
Vegetable peels are wet waste; plastic, glass and metal are dry.
So vegetable peels can go in.
Answer: Vegetable peels
quiz.mistake: Thinks any waste can become compost

quiz.q: Which living things help turn wet waste into compost?
quiz.explain: Earthworms and tiny living things in the soil break down wet waste.
steps: Earthworms and tiny living things break down wet waste.
So the answer is earthworms.
Answer: Earthworms
quiz.mistake: Does not know earthworms make compost

quiz.q: Why should we sort waste into wet and dry?
options: So wet waste becomes compost and dry waste can be recycled
So we can throw more waste
quiz.explain: Sorting makes it possible to compost and recycle waste.
steps: Sorted wet waste can become compost.
Sorted dry waste can be recycled.
So that is why we sort waste.
Answer: So wet waste becomes compost and dry waste can be recycled
quiz.mistake: Does not see the reason for sorting

quiz.q: Which colour bin is used for dry waste in many Indian cities?
quiz.explain: The blue bin is for dry waste like paper, plastic, glass and metal.
steps: The blue bin is for dry waste.
So the answer is blue.
Answer: Blue
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the bin colours

quiz.q: How is compost useful?
options: It makes the soil rich so plants grow well
It is used to make glass
quiz.explain: Compost adds goodness to the soil, like manure.
steps: Compost is a rich manure.
It makes the soil rich so plants grow well.
So that is how compost is useful.
Answer: It makes the soil rich so plants grow well
quiz.mistake: Does not know the use of compost

quiz.q: An empty milk packet should go into which bin?
quiz.explain: A milk packet is plastic. Rinse it and put it with dry waste.
steps: A milk packet is plastic, which is dry waste.
Dry waste goes in the dry waste bin.
So the answer is the dry waste bin.
Answer: The dry waste bin
quiz.mistake: Thinks a milk packet is wet waste because it held milk

teach.praise: Chirp! Wet waste becomes compost, and dry waste gets recycled!
teach.nudge: What can we make from wet waste?

revise.summary: Keep wet and dry waste in separate bins: green for wet and blue for dry in many cities. Wet waste can be turned into compost, a rich manure, with help from earthworms.
focus: Which bin colour is for which waste
remember: Green bin: wet waste; blue bin: dry waste
Compost = rich manure made from rotted wet waste
Put wet waste in a pit or pot, cover with soil or dry leaves, wait some weeks
traps: Don't put plastic, glass or metal in the compost pit.
A milk packet goes in the dry waste bin, not the wet bin.

learn.hook: Three magic words can shrink a mountain of garbage: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle!
points: Reduce means using fewer things so less waste is made, like carrying a cloth bag instead of taking plastic bags.
Reuse means using things again, like using a jam jar to store buttons.
Recycle means turning old things into new things. Old paper becomes new paper; old glass becomes new glass.
The kabadiwala buys old newspapers, bottles and metal and sends them for recycling.
Carry a steel water bottle and a tiffin box, and say no to single-use plastic.

example.q: Ananya's mother takes the same cloth bag to the vegetable market every day. How does this help cut down waste?
steps: She uses the same bag again and again — that is reusing the bag.
Because of this, she does not need new plastic bags, so less waste is made.
Not taking plastic bags means she is reducing waste.
example.answer: She reuses one cloth bag, so no new plastic bags end up as waste. This reduces waste.

learn.reallife: Count the plastic bags that come home in a week. Can your family bring that number down?

quiz.q: What does 'reduce' mean?
options: Use fewer things so less waste is made
quiz.explain: Reducing means making less waste in the first place.
steps: Reduce means using fewer things.
Then less waste is made.
So that is what 'reduce' means.
Answer: Use fewer things so less waste is made
quiz.mistake: Mixes up reduce and recycle

quiz.q: Using an old jam jar to store pencils is an example of ___.
quiz.explain: The jar is used again for a new job, so it is reused.
steps: Reuse means using things again.
The jam jar is used again to store pencils.
So it is reuse.
Answer: Reuse
quiz.mistake: Mixes up reuse and recycle

quiz.q: Old newspapers are made into new paper at a factory. This is ___.
quiz.explain: Turning old paper into new paper is recycling.
steps: Recycle means turning old things into new things.
Old newspapers become new paper.
So it is recycling.
Answer: Recycle
quiz.mistake: Mixes up recycle and reuse

quiz.q: Which habit helps reduce plastic waste?
options: Taking a new plastic bag every time
Using a new plastic plate for every snack
Carrying a cloth bag for shopping
quiz.explain: A cloth bag can be used many times, so fewer plastic bags are needed.
steps: A cloth bag can be used many times.
Then fewer plastic bags are needed.
So carrying a cloth bag reduces plastic waste.
Answer: Carrying a cloth bag for shopping
quiz.mistake: Does not link small habits with less waste

quiz.q: Who buys old newspapers, bottles and metal from homes so they can be recycled?
quiz.explain: The kabadiwala collects these things and sends them to be recycled.
steps: The kabadiwala buys old newspapers, bottles and metal.
He sends them for recycling.
So the answer is the kabadiwala.
Answer: The kabadiwala
quiz.mistake: Does not know who collects recyclable waste

quiz.q: Giving your old storybooks to a younger cousin is an example of ___.
quiz.explain: The books are used again by someone else, so they are reused.
steps: The storybooks are used again by someone else.
Using things again is reuse.
So it is reuse.
Answer: Reuse
quiz.mistake: Thinks reuse means only using things yourself

quiz.q: Which of these can be recycled?
quiz.explain: Glass can be melted and made into new glass. The others are wet waste for compost.
steps: Old glass can become new glass.
Peels, food and leaves are wet waste for compost.
So the glass bottle can be recycled.
Answer: A glass bottle
quiz.mistake: Mixes up recycling with composting

quiz.q: A family used to bring home 10 plastic bags a week. Now they bring only 4. By how many bags have they reduced their waste?
quiz.explain: 10 − 4 = 6 fewer plastic bags each week.
steps: Before: 10 bags
Now: 4 bags
Answer: 6
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference

teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Reduce, reuse, recycle — I will remember all three!

revise.summary: Reduce means using fewer things, reuse means using things again, and recycle means turning old things into new ones. The kabadiwala helps by sending old things for recycling.
focus: Telling reduce, reuse and recycle apart
remember: Reduce: use fewer things, like a cloth bag instead of plastic bags
Reuse: use again, like a jam jar for buttons
Recycle: old paper → new paper, old glass → new glass
Carry a steel bottle and tiffin; say no to single-use plastic
traps: Giving old books to a cousin is reuse, not recycle.
Food peels are composted, not recycled like glass.
